result.rationale: The migration directly interpolates legacy site setting values into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. A host value containing a single quote (the old setting was a free-text host list) would break/escape the SQL string, enabling SQL injection during migration. The old setting type was `host_list`, so arbitrary content is plausible. Real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The host values come from existing site settings (embeddable_hosts) which could contain single quotes or other SQL injection characters. If a malicious or accidental value like `evil.com'; DROP TABLE users; --` was stored in the settings, it would execute arbitrary SQL during migration. This is a real SQL injection vulnerability in the migration code.
